reference_authors: G Guichard; F Connan; R Graff; M Ostankovitch; S Muller; J G Guillet; J Choppin; J P Briand
reference_titles: Partially modified retro-inverso pseudopeptides as non-natural ligands for the human class I histocompatibility molecule HLA-A2.

mhc_export.assay__comments: The known HLA-A2-restricted epitope M58-66 from the matrix protein of influenza A virus was tested for its ability to promote the assembly of HLA-A2 molecules in T2 lysates.  M58-66 strongly promoted the assembly of HLA-A2 (approximately 330 fluorescence units), and the efficiency of stabilization occurred at a peptide concentration of 10nM or less (Figure 3).
mhc_export.reference__title: Partially modified retro-inverso pseudopeptides as non-natural ligands for the human class I histocompatibility molecule HLA-A2.
mhc_export.epitope__comments: The HLA-A2-restricted M58-66 epitope of the influenza A virus matrix protein was previously defined and described by Bednarek M et al. J Immunol 1991;147:4047-4053.
mhc_export.reference__authors: G Guichard; F Connan; R Graff; M Ostankovitch; S Muller; J G Guillet; J Choppin; J P Briand

reference_authors: G Guichard; F Connan; R Graff; M Ostankovitch; S Muller; J G Guillet; J Choppin; J P Briand
reference_titles: Partially modified retro-inverso pseudopeptides as non-natural ligands for the human class I histocompatibility molecule HLA-A2.

mhc_export.assay__comments: The retro-inverso peptide 1a was tested for its ability to promote the assembly of HLA-A2 molecules in T2 lysates.  Peptide 1a strongly promoted the assembly of HLA-A2 (approximately 375 fluorescence units), and demonstrated the highest efficiency of stabilization at peptide concentrations of 10nM or less (Figure 3).  This analog showed greater assembly strength and efficiency than the wild-type M58-66.
mhc_export.reference__title: Partially modified retro-inverso pseudopeptides as non-natural ligands for the human class I histocompatibility molecule HLA-A2.
mhc_export.epitope__comments: Retro-inverso peptide 1a is an analog if the known HLA-A2-restricted epitope M58-66 of influenza A virus.  The Psi (Ψ) NH-CO modification of this peptide was obtained by replacement of two sequential amino acids with a (S), or (R, S)-2-isobutylmalonic acid derivative and a gem-diaminoalkyl residue.
mhc_export.reference__authors: G Guichard; F Connan; R Graff; M Ostankovitch; S Muller; J G Guillet; J Choppin; J P Briand
